segments.blurb: Long Heathrow layover (land 6:35am, fly out 2:40pm). Plan: M&S + Harrods. Sat — verify store hours; be back at LHR ~2h before departure. Both M&S and Harrods have shops inside Heathrow if you skip the city run.
Land 5:45pm on the 7th; full day the 8th to explore before Nice on the 9th. Jet-lag buffer built in.
Anniversary 11/9. Le Sens 11/10. Le Plongeoir + Chagall 11/11 (holiday). Monaco + Èze 11/12.

Thu 11/12 — ~20 min train from Nice (moved from Wed 11/11: no trains + holiday buses that day). Monaco-Ville + F1 circuit walk into a Café de Paris lunch, casino, then bus 602 up to Èze for late-afternoon light and back to Nice.

Venice overnight mid-block; Monza + Como day trip. Hold room over Venice night. Duplicate Milan hold is canceled; 43 Station is the Milan base. Shopping: Quadrilatero della Moda (Montenapoleone), Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II, La Rinascente, Corso Buenos Aires; Como silk on the Monza/Como day.
Daypack only; big bags stay in held Milan room.
Four overplanned, skippable days: Strasbourg/Colmar, Freiburg/Black Forest, Lucerne + weather-dependent mountain, and Basel city/Jewish history/football.

Two full days: watches + Lindt + Christmas markets on 11/24, then Rhine Falls or a relaxed Zurich/market day on 11/25. 11/26 travel day. Shopping: Bahnhofstrasse, Zurich HB/Sechseläutenplatz Christmas markets, and Freitag flagship in Zürich-West.
Break the transatlantic haul; US pre-clearance at DUB.

items.text: Land LHR — clear UK border
Breakfast: The Ivy Kensington Brasserie — RESERVATION CONFIRMED, 2 (veggie full English for Nicole + full English for Max, pot of tea)
London layover: M&S + Harrods (opens ~10am Sat). Backup: M&S + Harrods shops inside Heathrow
LHR → MRS (land 5:45p)
Check in Residhotel Vieux Port (4 Rue Coutellerie — 5 min walk to the port)
Dinner: Le Bar de la Marine — casual Vieux Port bistro (the 1929 Pagnol-trilogy setting), 15 Quai de Rive Neuve. Easy jet-lag first night, open late; ~12 min walk around the port from the hotel
Slow jet-lag morning — coffee & pastry on the Vieux Port
Vieux Port stroll: daily fish market on Quai des Belges + Foster's mirror-canopy Ombrière; then La Maison du Pastis (Quai du Port) — Max tastes & buys a proper Marseille pastis
🛍 Le Panier — Marseille's oldest quarter: savon-de-Marseille soap shops, artisan & ceramic boutiques (open Sun afternoon), street art, Place des Moulins, La Vieille Charité courtyard

MuCEM — Museum of European & Mediterranean Civilisations: Rudy Ricciotti's lacework-concrete J4 on the water, linked to Fort Saint-Jean by a rooftop footbridge. Open daily exc Tue ~11:00–18:00, €11 (Sun 11/8 = open)
Fort Saint-Jean gardens & footbridge, Cathédrale de la Major (striped Byzantine), and the shops/terraces under Les Voûtes de la Major
Notre-Dame de la Garde ('La Bonne Mère') for the sunset panorama over the whole city & sea — bus 60 or petit-train up, walk down (sunset ~5:15p)

Apéritif at Vallon des Auffes — pastis + a plate of panisses (fried chickpea sticks) on the quay of the tiny fishing cove, boats bobbing, then a 2-min stroll to dinner. No backtrack to the port; comes straight off the Notre-Dame descent along the corniche
Dinner: Chez Fonfon — bouillabaisse at the Vallon des Auffes cove ✅ RESERVED (2 pers, 8:00 PM)

items.text: Dinner in Vieux Nice — Niçois specialties (pick your spot below). Holiday: call ahead to confirm they're open on 11/11.
items.detail: Leaning daube niçoise, petits farcis, stockfish. If peckish earlier, grab socca at a Cours Saleya stand or Chez Pipo by the port (right near Le Plongeoir).

options.name: Antibes half-day
options.booking: ~25 min each way by TER (Nice-Ville → Antibes). Trains WEST of Nice are not affected by the works, but it's a holiday timetable (fewer trains) — check SNCF Connect the day before. No booking needed.
options.detail: Early train to Antibes: Musée Picasso in the Château Grimaldi on the ramparts, then graze the Marché Provençal (covered market, Cours Masséna) — Provençal produce, cheeses, socca and a slice of pissaladière on the go. Back in Nice by ~11:15 for the noon Le Plongeoir booking. Holiday: confirm Musée Picasso + market hours for 11/11 before going.

options.name: Relaxed Nice / Villefranche
options.booking: No booking. Villefranche-sur-Mer is east of Nice (no trains before ~17:30 today) — bus 100 or skip; Cours Saleya / Old Town is the easy pick.
options.detail: Slow start. Stay in Nice and graze Cours Saleya (flower + produce market most mornings) and Rue Pairolière — socca, pan-bagnat, pissaladière, no sit-down needed. Fully cancelable if you'd rather do nothing before lunch.

options.detail: Cult micro-spot (4 Rue Raoul Bosio) from an ex-Michelin chef — stockfish, tripes, pissaladière, farcis. No reservations, no cards, ~a dozen seats.

★ Walk the F1 circuit into lunch: Port Hercule harbour straight → Sainte-Dévote → climb Beau Rivage → Casino Square; Fairmont Hairpin + tunnel entrance are 5 min below the casino.

🚌 ZOU! 602 Èze Village 17:55 → Nice Vauban 18:30 (backup: 20:10 → 20:40, the LAST bus). Tram T1 from Vauban back to the hotel area.

dining.name: Confiserie Sprüngli

dining.name: Trattoria San Giacomo (Bellagio)

EU purchases (France/Italy/Ireland): ask for tax-free/VAT refund paperwork at the store, keep goods unused and accessible, and validate the forms with EU customs at Dublin Airport before the final Dublin→Philadelphia departure. Switzerland purchases: separate process — ask the Swiss store for tax-free paperwork, meet any Swiss minimum purchase threshold, and validate/export at Zurich Airport when leaving Switzerland for Dublin. Do NOT pack refund goods in checked bags until after the relevant customs validation; photograph receipts/forms as backup. Worth doing mainly for watches/jewelry/luxury goods, not small souvenirs.

options.label: Le Bar de la Marine
options.desc: Iconic Pagnol café-brasserie on the Vieux Port (15 Quai de Rive Neuve) — casual terrace, classic Marseillais plates. Perfect first-night spot for Max's pastis; ask for panisses. Open daily; ~10 min stroll or hop the little César ferry across the port.

options.label: Place de Lenche terrace (Le Panier)
options.desc: The closest + most local option — pizzas & Provençal plates on a tiny Le Panier square, ~4 min uphill from the hotel. Super casual, pastis on the terrace.

options.label: Toinou Les Fruits de Mer
options.desc: The real Marseille one at 3 Cours Saint-Louis (~8 min walk — NOT the Aix-en-Provence branch on toinou.com). Bright shellfish brasserie, open daily & late, walk-in — if you'd rather do oysters night one.

options.label: Les Halles de la Major
options.desc: Waterfront food hall under the cathedral arches (Les Voûtes de la Major) — a proper oyster bar plus seafood, charcuterie & Provençal stalls. Open daily incl. Sun, buzzy and casual, right on the Le Panier→MuCEM walk. Oysters + wine for Max; seafood/veg spread for Nicole.

options.label: Le Môle Passédat (MuCEM rooftop)
options.desc: 3-star chef Gérald Passédat's restaurant atop MuCEM with a panoramic sea & fort terrace — flows straight into your 2pm MuCEM visit. Fish-forward, scenic splurge. ⚠️ Verify Sun lunch service in Nov.

options.desc: Classic Provençal terrace right on Quai du Port, steps from the hotel — aïoli, grilled catch, pieds paquets for Max. ⚠️ Verify Sun opening.

options.label: Maison Saint Honoré
options.desc: One of Marseille's best bakeries (near Cours d'Estienne d'Orves) — superb viennoiserie, coffee & a light breakfast. Casual, reliable on a Monday, and on the way to the Rue St-Ferréol shops before the train.

options.label: Café de l'Abbaye (Saint-Victor)
options.desc: Terrace with a postcard view across the Vieux Port to Notre-Dame — a relaxed final-morning sit-down. ~12 min south of the hotel; leave time to get back for the 1:04p train.

options.label: Les Bords de Mer (rooftop)
